title: Risk-adjusted Launch Lanes and Regional Blackout Windows for Release Cadence
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a risk-adjusted launch lane framework that formalizes regional blackout windows, capacity harmonization signals, and gating criteria across runtime/console/API releases. This ticket scopes the policy, runbooks, simulation plan, and stakeholder approvals needed to adopt launch lanes for Q2 releases and beyond.
goals: Define 3 launch lanes (Green: low-risk, Amber: monitored, Red: constrained) with quantitative gates
Specify regional blackout windows and overlap rules for multi-region capacity-sensitive changes
Create automated signals (latency P50/P95, error rate, capacity headroom, cost-per-token delta) to drive lane assignments
Deliver a playbook + runbook for product, SRE, and capacity planning to use during weekly runways
deliverables: Launch lane policy doc (ownership, criteria, rollback thresholds)
Runbook: how to schedule blackout windows and request exceptions
Simulation report: 3 scenarios (normal, holiday-peak, infra-degradation) with suggested lane mappings
Dashboard templates: lane health, regional headroom, gating signal history
Stakeholder sign-off and a pilot with two upcoming runtime/console releases
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc reviewed and approved by Product, SRE, Capacity, and Legal
Runbook includes step-by-step rollback and canary rules tied to lane signals
Simulation shows >=90% of pilot releases would have been placed in the correct lane given historical data
Dashboards surface lane assignment and gate breaches in <5 minutes and are wired to Slack alerts
Pilot completed with one runtime release and one console release without unexpected capacity incidents
comments: 2026-02-12 — Kickoff: aligned with SRE and Capacity. Decided to model three lanes instead of four to reduce cognitive load.
2026-02-18 — Data request submitted to Observability team for historical P95 latency, error rates, and regional capacity usage (last 12 months). Owner: Priya Raman.
2026-02-25 — Trade-off note from SRE: tighter P95 thresholds reduce rollout velocity; proposed making P95 breaches require manual review only in Green lane.
2026-03-03 — Design reviewed dashboard mockups. PM feedback: surface cost-per-token delta prominently to catch quantization/quantized-model regressions.
2026-03-08 — Decision: Blackout windows will be region-scoped and time-boxed (max 6 hours) with an exception workflow for critical security patches.
2026-03-10 — Action item: ENG to run simulation #2 (holiday-peak) and produce heatmap. Assigned to Maya Chen. Due 2026-03-18.
2026-03-12 — Legal requested an audit trail for blackout approvals; adding an 'approval_id' field to runbook steps and integrating with console audit logs.
Open follow-ups: finalize lane naming (we currently use Green/Amber/Red internally), schedule pilot releases, and add Slack alert thresholds to SLO playbooks.
